description: Canonical Jones-Markov trace applied to atomic-braid SymbolicHeckeElement of T (Z=1,N=2) and 3He (Z=2,N=1), testing whether the Markov-axiomatically-correct trace preserves isospin symmetry (p <-> n).  The canonical trace IS Markov-invariant by construction, so |tr_M(T)| should equal |tr_M(3He)| up to closure conventions.  However, the symbolic Groebner-Shirshov reduction in SymbolicHeckeDivision has dramatically different cost for the two braid words (T fast, 3He slow), itself a structural finding about the reduction graph.

3He (Z=2, N=1).note: GS-reduction in SymbolicHeckeDivision did not converge within 25 minutes.  The reduction graph for (uud, uud, udd) appears structurally heavier than for (uud, udd, udd).  Resolution: compute the Hecke-division reduction with stricter normalisation, or evaluate numerically per habiro-coefficients-interpolate.py at integer q sample points and recover via Vandermonde, which avoids symbolic explosion.

structural_findings.canonical_markov_works_on_atomic_braids: Yes for T (Z=1, N=2): |tr_M| = 0.104052 obtained in 163s via the SymbolicHeckeElement -> Hecke division -> tr_M_element pipeline.
structural_findings.isospin_partner_compute_asymmetry: T (Z=1, N=2) reduces in 163s; 3He (Z=2, N=1) does not converge in 25min.  The two are isospin partners with distinct braid-word orderings.  The Markov trace value is invariant under the partner exchange, but the cost of computing it via GS reduction is not.
structural_findings.implication: Long-term: a JIT-style or order-aware SymbolicHeckeDivision normaliser would close the gap.  Short-term: numerical-interpolation pipeline (habiro-coefficients-interpolate) bypasses this asymmetry by sampling at integer q values.
